title: Combining Conditions
description: Combine several conditions in one check using and, or, and not.

content.text: You can go to the park only if it is sunny **and** your homework is done. Some decisions depend on more than one thing.

items.sub: At least one must be True.
Flips True to False, and False to True.

content.value: Flip the switches below to see what each one does.

content.question: It is sunny, but your homework is not done. Is `sunny and homework_done` True?
content.explain: `and` needs both sides to be True. One False makes the whole thing False.

items.title: and
items.code:
True and True    # True
True and False   # False
False and False  # False
items.text: True only when **both** sides are True. A single False makes the whole thing False.

items.title: or
items.code:
True or True     # True
True or False    # True
False or False   # False
items.text: True when **at least one** side is True. False only when both are False.

content.value:
sunny = True
homework_done = True

if sunny and homework_done:
    print("You can go to the park!")

has_cookie = True
has_cake = False

if has_cookie or has_cake:
    print("You have a sweet treat!")
output: You can go to the park!

content.question: What does `True or False` give?
content.explain: `or` needs just one side to be True, and the left side is.

parts.label: flip
parts.note: Takes a single value and turns it into the opposite.

items.title: Works, but wordy
items.text: Compares a boolean to `True`. Extra work.

items.title: Cleaner
items.text: `sunny` already holds True or False. This means the same thing and reads better.

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: `or` needs only one True side. `has_key` is True, so the whole thing is `True`.
content.code:
has_key = True
knows_code = False
print(has_key or knows_code)

items: Mix `and`, `or`, `not` with the comparisons from earlier.
You can combine more than two at once.
Use parentheses `( )` when you want to be sure which part is worked out first.

content.code:
raining = True
has_umbrella = False
if raining and not has_umbrella:
    print("You will get wet!")

steps.note: Work out `not has_umbrella` first: `not False` is `True`. Then `True and True` is True.
The condition was True, so the block runs.

content.title: Work out the condition
content.outro: `not` is applied to its value before `and` combines the two sides.

content.value:
age = 15
has_ticket = True

if age >= 12 and has_ticket:
    print("Enjoy the film!")

raining = True
has_umbrella = False

if raining and not has_umbrella:
    print("You will get wet!")

money = 3
is_member = True
print((money >= 5) or is_member)
content.caption: Parentheses make it clear the comparison is worked out first.

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: `age >= 12` is True, but `has_ticket` is False. `and` needs both, so the condition is False and `else` runs.

quiz.question: Which operator needs BOTH sides to be True?
quiz.explain: and needs both sides to be True. or needs only one side, and not flips a single value.

quiz.question: If raining = True, what does 'not raining' give you?
quiz.explain: not flips the value. Since raining is True, not raining becomes False.

quiz.question: What is the result of: False or True
quiz.explain: or only needs one side to be True. The right side is True, so the whole thing is True.
